## Continuing a video (EXPERIMENTAL FEATURE)

### Enable continuation
Set **Normal / Continue to ON** and enter the previous video’s local file path.

Keep the prompt consistent with the existing scene and describe what should happen next. The source must contain at least the selected number of guide frames.

With Continue OFF, the source video and continuation controls are ignored.

### Audio and optional image reference
- **Previous video has audio:** ON preserves its soundtrack; OFF supplies silence for the previous section.
- **Use source AUDIO guide:** ON also uses the ending soundtrack to guide the new audio. Requires a source with audio. OFF keeps video guidance without audio guidance.
- **Use last source frame as H3 reference:** ON adds the final source frame as an extra image reference.

The automatic image reference follows after the main image and any enabled additional images in **Additional references**. With all image loaders bypassed, it will be the `<Picture 1>` reference. If the main image reference or any of the additional ones is enabled, this last source frame will always become the last reference (`<Picture N+1>` where N is the number of enabled reference images).

### Length and stitching
**Duration in secs — Preview + Full** applies to both modes and includes the guide window. Only the portion after that window is appended.

All previous video frames are retained. The overlapping beginning of the NEW video and audio is removed before joining them to the source.

### Output folder
**Extension output subfolder** chooses the destination relative to ComfyUI’s output directory, for example `video/extensions`.

It affects Continue mode only and preserves the selected Full/Preview filename. The saved file contains the complete stitched video.

### Guide window: 22 / 39 / 56 frames
This selects how much of the previous video’s ending guides the new generation.

| Frames | Context at 24 fps |
|---|---|
| 22 | About 0.92 seconds |
| 39 | About 1.63 seconds |
| 56 | About 2.33 seconds |

A longer window gives the model more context, with additional processing and memory demand. It may improve continuity, but does not guarantee identical appearance, lighting or voice.

The selected window is used by both sampling passes and by the optional audio guide. Overlap trimming updates automatically.

## Basic generation

### Getting started
Set **Normal / Continue to OFF** for a new video. Write your prompt, choose the aspect ratio, resolution and duration, then generate.

Use **Preview ON** to test the first pass. Switch it OFF for the complete two-pass result.

Main quality selectors are: Enable/Disable sparsity, second pass steps and resolution.
- Default/fast: VSA Enabled and 3 steps refining second stage.
- Quality: Sparse node bypassed and 4-6 steps refining second stage. Additional steps on first pass might add some additional detail and better audio, but above 8 you get diminishing returns.
- If your machine allows for that: Bumping first pass to 0.4mpx and then second refining stage can easily go beyond 1mpx to 1.2mpx or more.

### Models and references
- **Diffusion model:** the H3 checkpoint that generates the video and audio. Use a model compatible with this workflow’s Turbo sampling setup.
- **Text encoder:** interprets the prompt and references. The CLIP loader’s type should be **minimax**.
- **Video VAE / Audio VAE:** convert between the model’s internal representation and the finished video or soundtrack. Keep them in their respective loaders.
- **Turbo LoRA:** leave bypassed when the checkpoint already includes Turbo. Enable it only when the chosen model requires the separate Turbo LoRA.
- **Additional LoRAs:** optional effects or adaptations. Enable the desired rows and adjust their strengths.
- **Load Image:** enable for a manual image reference; bypass for generation without one. Refer to the manual image as `<Picture 1>` in the prompt.

Describe the subject, scene, action, camera and desired sound or dialogue in the prompt.

### Additional references
The **Additional references** panel contains three image, three video and three standalone audio loaders. They start empty and bypassed. Choose a file and unbypass only the loaders you want to use; leave unused loaders bypassed. These references feed H3 conditioning in both Normal and Continue modes.

Video loaders supply **24 FPS frames and their paired soundtracks**. Use short reference clips (2–15 seconds). For a silent reference video, disconnect its soundtrack wire from the generation subgraph before enabling it; VHS cannot extract audio from a video without an audio track. The separate audio loaders provide standalone references, not replacement video soundtracks.

In the prompt use `<Picture N>`, `<Video N>` and `<Audio N>` for the enabled references. Pictures are ordered: main image, enabled additional images 1–3, then the optional continuation source frame. Bypassed images do not occupy a picture number. Video soundtracks are numbered as audio references before the enabled standalone audio files. More references increase conditioning work and memory use.

### Optional RefMods
The **Additional references - RefMods** panel loads pre-made reference `.safetensors` from `ComfyUI/models/refmods/`. Requires **ComfyUI-MiniMaxH3Mod**. Select a file and adjust its strength; **(none)** or strength **0** disables a slot. Choose **Visual**, **Audio** or **All** for the desired components. The first slot starts at Visual; additional slots use the pack's All default.

RefMods are applied once to conditioning shared by both sampling passes, in Normal and Continue modes. They supplement the existing references and continuation guides. Describe the subject in the prompt; filenames and `<Subject N>` do not automatically bind characters to RefMod slots. Audio references are supported, but reliable voice cloning is not established. Start with one copy; additional tokens increase processing and memory use.

### Resolution and duration
- **Selector First LowRes Pass:** sets the aspect ratio and first-pass resolution. Keep the dimension multiple at **32**.
- **Final Target Megapixels:** sets the second-pass resolution before RTX upscaling.
- **Duration in secs — Preview + Full:** requested generation length in both modes. Preview saves the first-pass result; Full adds the learned latent upscale and refinement.

The first pass establishes the video at lower resolution. The learned latent upscaler increases its resolution, and the second pass refines it. Larger resolutions and longer clips require more processing and memory.

H3 generation is **24 fps**. Continue output is always **24 fps**; Normal output uses the FrameGen multiplier. H3 rounds duration to its supported frame counts, so the actual length can be slightly longer than requested.

### Preview, seed and audio
- **Preview ON:** skips the learned latent upscale and second sampling pass. Export uses the first-pass video.
- **Preview OFF:** runs both passes.
- **Seed (rgthree):** `-1` chooses a new random seed. Use a fixed number when comparing changes.
- **Use first pass audio ON:** exports the first-pass soundtrack.
- **Use first pass audio OFF:** exports the second-pass soundtrack. Preview always uses first-pass audio.

**Reusing a preview:** Generate with Preview ON and a fixed seed, then switch Preview OFF while keeping the first-pass inputs unchanged. If ComfyUI still holds the cached result, Full mode can reuse the first-pass latent and proceed directly to the learned latent upscaler and refinement. Changing the prompt, seed, duration, first-pass resolution, model, sampling settings or conditioning requires a new first pass.

**ModelPreviewOverrideKJ** controls the live display during sampling. Its resolution, JPEG quality and Tiny VAE settings do not set the final video’s resolution or export quality.

### Sampling and advanced controls
- **Steps:** number of sampling iterations.
- **Sampler / Scheduler:** control how sampling progresses.
- **Scheduler Second Pass:** controls the refinement stage’s noise range using a scheduler (use Scheduler or manual, not both).
- **Manual Second Pass Sigmas:** controls the refinement stage’s noise range manually (use Scheduler or manual, not both).
- **Video / Audio sigma shifts:** adjust the respective noise schedules.
- **Attention backend / BlockSparseAttention:** advanced execution and speed/quality choices.

Use the working sampling configuration as a starting point and change one setting at a time when comparing results.

### Upscaling and saving
**RTX Video Super Resolution** runs after decoding and can further increase the exported resolution. Bypass it to retain the decoded resolution.

Edit the **Full Resolution** and **Preview** filename-prefix boxes to choose filenames and folders, relative to ComfyUI’s output directory. The final Save Video node writes the MP4.

### RTX FrameGen multiplier and output FPS
FrameGen is for **Normal mode only**. The integer **FrameGen multiplier** sets both interpolation and export FPS: **1× skips FrameGen and saves 24 FPS; 2× / 3× / 4× / 5× save 48 / 72 / 96 / 120 FPS**. Use values **1–5** and keep the RTX node active in **frame rate multiplier** mode. **Use 1× to disable interpolation instead of manually bypassing RTX**; bypassing it with a higher multiplier would mismatch playback speed. **Continue automatically skips FrameGen and remains at 24 FPS**, including source loading and stitched export. H3 generation stays at 24 FPS. Higher multipliers increase processing and frame memory. RTX returns `(N−1)×multiplier+1` frames; its native endpoint behavior is unchanged and no padding is added.

### Optional output grain — Lokken pilot
**Requires [Lokken VideoTools](https://registry.comfy.org/nodes/lokken-videotools)**, available through ComfyUI Manager. Install the pack and restart ComfyUI. **Output grain strength — 0 = OFF** is in Sampling and output settings. Leave the control active: use **0** to disable grain, or increase in **0.001** steps. Start low and adjust to taste; 0.005 to 0.010 recommended. Do not bypass the strength control.

Grain is added after RTX/FrameGen and overlap trimming, during encoding. Normal and Preview affect the current clip; Continue affects only the retained new segment. The source segment is encoded with grain OFF. For matching texture, use grain from the first clip. The grain pattern is random and has no fixed-seed control. Audio, dimensions, frame counts and FPS are unchanged.

### Output saving quality
**Output saving quality — encoder preset**, below the second-pass scheduler, controls the video H264 encoder quality. Faster values might produce bigger result files and worse output quality, while slower values will generate beter H264 videos but with longer running times. Default: **medium**. Leave this control active.

# RTX FRAME GENERATION
## EXPERIMENTAL FEATURE

## NORMAL MODE ONLY (NO CONTINUATION ACTIVE)

**FrameGen is incompatible with continuation in this workflow.** Continue automatically skips it and always loads/exports video at **24 FPS**, regardless of the multiplier.

### ONE CONTROL: FRAMEGEN MULTIPLIER
- **1×:** FrameGen skipped, **24 FPS**
- **2× / 3× / 4× / 5×:** FrameGen enabled, **48 / 72 / 96 / 120 FPS**

**Use values 1–5. Keep the RTX node active in frame rate multiplier mode; use 1× to turn interpolation off.** The control sets both RTX interpolation and export FPS. H3 generation always stays at **24 FPS**.

Other values will give you errors

RTX Frame Generation is compute and memory hungry. Have this in mind when enabling this option in modest spec machines.

## Optional RefMods
Requires **ComfyUI-MiniMaxH3Mod**. Restart ComfyUI after installation.

Put saved RefMod `.safetensors` files in `ComfyUI/models/refmods/`, then refresh node definitions. Select a file in the loader. Use **+ Add RefMod** for additional slots.

- **(none)** or **strength 0** disables a slot. Leave the loader active.
- Start with **one copy**. Strength controls the reference influence.
- **Visual** loads appearance references; **Audio** loads audio references; **All** loads both from combined bundles. The first slot starts at Visual; new slots use the pack's All default.
- Injection is inside the generation subgraph and feeds **both passes**, in **Normal and Continue** modes. Existing continuation video/audio guides remain connected.

Describe the desired subject in the prompt. Filenames and `<Subject N>` are not automatic triggers. Existing numbered tags apply to the ordinary reference loaders, not automatic bindings to these added RefMods.

Conflicting references can alter appearance or sound. Voice cloning is not established. More tokens/copies increase inference cost. This panel loads existing RefMods; it does not create them.

If you need to modify the application and conditioning node, it is placed inside the "Conditioning and generation" subgraph, next to the main ref2av Minimax node.
